user.title: AI Workspace
user.description: Shared settings for the chat. Next, add your first assistant (Cursor, OpenAI, Ollama, and others) from the integration page.

data.tts_natural: Natural speech for text to speech
data.enable_sidebar: Show AI Workspace in the sidebar

data_description.stt_engine: Browser dictation needs a secure site (https). Or choose a Home Assistant speech-to-text engine under Settings. The browser must allow the microphone.
data_description.tts_engine: Piper, Google Translate, or a voice from one of your AI assistants. Off keeps replies as text only.
data_description.speak_replies: When a voice is selected, each reply is read as it arrives. Off keeps the speaker button so you can play a reply yourself.
data_description.tts_natural: On by default. Removes formatting so read-aloud sounds natural. Off reads the message exactly as written.
data_description.enable_sidebar: Shows AI Workspace in the sidebar. When off, administrators can still open the full page if they use its menu link.
data_description.enable_overlay: Turns the floating AI button on or off. On Settings pages it sits higher so it does not cover system buttons.
data_description.allow_users: Non-admin users can open the floating chat with the same Home Assistant access as their account. Off: administrators only. The full AI Workspace page in the sidebar stays admin-only.
data_description.house_map: Optional. Helps explain how one item is wired (what triggers it, what it affects). Off by default. For live on/off state or full lists, ask the assistant to check Home Assistant.
data_description.shorten_mcp_results: On by default. Very long answers from Home Assistant (whole-home lists, big searches) are summarized before they go to the AI. That saves tokens and keeps replies snappy. Off sends the full text.
data_description.change_history: On by default. Keeps a record of configuration changes the assistant made so you can review or undo them in Change History. Off stops new entries; the assistant can still use Home Assistant.
data_description.track_usage: On by default. Records tokens and estimated USD cost after each Cursor or cloud turn. Shows a Usage page in the chat. Off stops new records; existing history stays.
data_description.show_chat_usage: On by default. Shows tokens and cost under the chat title. Off hides only that line; tracking and the Usage page stay.
data_description.ha_usage_sensors: Off by default. Creates cost, token, and turn sensors on a Usage device and on each agent for your own dashboards. Off removes those sensors.
data_description.low_token: How much each turn sends, for every Cloud / Ollama / Azure agent.
data_description.prompt_cache: On by default. Claude needs this to cache the repeated tool list; GPT often caches on its own. Cursor and Ollama ignore it. Leave it on so later rounds of a turn cost less.
data_description.ui_theme: Off by default. When on, only Home Assistant UI components are used which may work better with themes.
data_description.cross_chat: Off by default. When on, a question can use another chat whose title shares words with it. You do not have to mention chat. A short excerpt only, and that chat is not changed.
data_description.keep_chats: Newest unpinned chats to keep per person. Pinned chats are always kept. Default 30.

data_description.mcp_kind: Servers this Home Assistant can reach. Pick Custom to enter your own address.
data_description.mcp_token: Built-in: long-lived access token, or leave empty to use your current login. HA-MCP: usually empty. Vibecode: agent key. Custom: only if that server asks for a key.

data_description.system_prompt: Tone and habits only. Leave empty for the default. The assistant always keeps access to Home Assistant and quick links in replies.

error.no_runtime: Cannot reach the Cursor runtime. Start it and check the address on this form.
error.invalid_auth: The provider rejected this API key.
error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the provider. Check the URL and the network.

user.title: Connection
user.description: Pick how this assistant connects to Home Assistant and other services.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Another service the assistant can use during chat.

data_description.name: A short name, such as Directus. The assistant uses it to tell this connection from the others.
data_description.url: Web address (https://…). Discovered servers are filled in automatically.
data_description.token: Only if that server asks for a key. Leave empty when editing to keep the saved key.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Choose the provider. The next screen asks only for what that provider needs.

data_description.api_provider: Cursor, or a cloud or local model.

provider_cursor.title: Cursor
provider_cursor.description: Cursor address, API key, model, and response speed.

data_description.runtime_token: Same password as on your Cursor runtime. Leave empty when using the add-on with automatic pairing.
data_description.cursor_api_key: From your Cursor account (Integrations). Leave blank when editing to keep the saved key.
data_description.model: Pick from the list or type a model name. Empty uses Composer.
data_description.effort: How much thinking time to allow. Composer defaults to Fast.
data_description.assist: Also lists this assistant under Home Assistant Assist (voice). Off keeps it in AI Workspace chat only and removes what it added to Assist.

provider_cloud.title: Cloud agent
provider_cloud.description: This agent keeps its own key. Copy one from an integration that is already set up, or paste a new one. Leave the key blank when editing to keep the saved key.

data_description.borrow: Uses the key already stored by that integration. The other integration is left as it is.
data_description.api_key: Your key from the AI provider, not your Home Assistant login.
data_description.model: Pick from the list or type a model name. Empty uses the provider default.
data_description.effort: Fast, High, or High fast when the model supports it.
data_description.check_house: On by default for Off. The assistant looks up Home Assistant before answering about your setup (not for simple greetings). Light always checks. Medium and Extreme ignore this. Turn off if your model already does that on its own.
data_description.assist: Also lists this assistant under Home Assistant Assist (voice). Off keeps it in AI Workspace chat only and removes what it added to Assist.
data_description.assist_stt: Adds a Speech-to-text option in Home Assistant using this assistant's key. Off removes what it added.
data_description.stt_model: Leave empty for the provider default. You can type another model name if yours offers one.
data_description.assist_tts: Adds a Text-to-speech option in Home Assistant using this assistant's key. Off removes what it added.
data_description.tts_model: Leave empty for the default voice model. You can type another name if your provider lists one.
data_description.tts_voice: Coral is the default. Voices work for the languages you set under Assist → Language.
data_description.tts_speed: How fast this voice speaks. 1× is normal. Applies to AI Workspace and Assist.

provider_ollama.title: Ollama
provider_ollama.description: Point this at the Ollama server.

data_description.model: Pick from the list or type a model you installed. Empty uses llama3.2.
data_description.effort: Used when the model supports it.
data_description.check_house: On by default for Off. The assistant looks up Home Assistant before answering about your setup (not for simple greetings). Light always checks. Medium and Extreme ignore this. Turn off if your model already does that on its own.
data_description.assist: Also lists this assistant under Home Assistant Assist (voice). Off keeps it in AI Workspace chat only and removes what it added to Assist.

data_description.api_key: The Azure OpenAI key. Leave blank when editing to keep the saved key.
data_description.azure_api_version: Leave the default unless Azure support gave you another version.

data_description.assist: Also lists this assistant under Home Assistant Assist (voice). Off keeps it in AI Workspace chat only and removes what it added to Assist.
